newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds down, could slip more on US rates.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds down, could slip more on US rates.

text.p: Argentine bonds fell Friday on U.S. interest rate fears after strong U.S. producer price figures pointed to inflationary pressures.
Traders said the market could fall more as the PPI report upped the uncertainties over how much and when the U.S. Federal Reserve will next hike rates.
One trader said the best for the market could be a hike in May, taking away the uncertainty, but even so there could be more losses.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down 5/8 at 88-5/8.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.10 to 127.85.
Despite the decline Friday, "institutional investors were not selling," said the trader.

With rising worries over U.S. rates, the market was seen continuing its U.S. indictor vigil next week, said another trader. Tuesday's release of consumer price figures were seen as next week's main event.
In the money markets, call money rates were flat at 5.83 percent.
